Author: Deepak Verma
Bench: Deepak Verma
HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 78 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 21832 of 2022 Applicant :- Mohit Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

entities.label: COURT

entities.text: CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 21832 of 2022

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Abhishek Gupta,Durga Prasad Tiwari,Vinay Prakash Shukla Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sheel Kumar Ojha Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the informant and perused the record.

The instant bail application has been filed with a prayer to release the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 148 of 2022, registered under Sections 323, 504, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B of I.P.C., Police Station Ecotech-3, District Gautam Budh Nagar, during pendency of the trial.

entities.text: Police Station Ecotech-3, District Gautam Budh Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
It is argued that offences are triable by Magistrate.
F.I.R. is delayed by seven months.
It is submitted that the parties have arrived to settlement.
The applicant has undertaken to return entire amount which was deposited in his account.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 01.05.2022.
In case, the applicant is released on bail,hewill not misuse the liberty of bail and co-operate in trial.

Mohit vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147332161/
1
Per contra learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for grant of bail of the applicant, but on proposal of depositing the amount he has not made opposition.

Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of offence, evidence, complicity of accused and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and the law laid down by the Apex Court inSatendra Kumar Antil Vs. C.B.I. & Another,S.L.P.(Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: inSatendra Kumar Antil Vs. C.B.I. & Another,S.L.P.(Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant, Mohit, who is involved in the aforesaid case crime, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/ pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
2. The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
3. The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
It is, however, provided that in case the applicant fails to repay or the cheques are dishonored, it is open to the informant to make recall of this order.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

Order Date :- 21.2.2023 Virendra  Mohit vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147332161/
